messages.author: 8d4d06c10c4d67c9
messages.subject: Mode-jumping
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering whether there's any mode-jumping option implemented in rstan (I think my data gives rise to this problem) ? If so, is it specified by default or does it have to be specified by the user?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mode-jumping
parts:
By default, Stan is attempting to sample from the posterior distribution. It does not provide a point estimate (like optimization) or an approximation of your posterior distribution (algorithms like EP or VB). If there are multiple modes in the posterior, than Stan, like any other correct MCMC algorithm, "should" sample from the posterior in the limit. Have you taken a look at some of the built-in convergence diagnostics, split R-hat and estimated number of effective samples? Have you visualized the samples themselves? (The alternative is to just look at the output of print.) If you haven't, that's the place to start.

With regards to non-identifiable models, there are sections in the manual that discuss this issue and some suggestions on how to deal with it. I would also recommend the Gelman and Hill book on multilevel models.

So, the answer you're looking for is yes. But since Stan's default sampling algorithm, NUTS, isn't trying to search for a mode, there is no concept of turning mode-jumping on or off.

Hopefully that helps.



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mode-jumping
parts:
Sampling from highly (or even mildly) multimodal posteriors
is a very tricky business, especially in high dimensions.

I'm afraid we don't have anything in Stan such as
tempering or ensemble methods to help with mode jumping.
Nor is anything like this going to be added in the near
future unless someone volunteers and implements it for us.

- Bob
